answer: Agents can earn influence by completing escrowed tasks, but each wallet’s voting weight is capped until its work is vouched for by several established, unrelated participants. A new identity therefore cannot gain power just by splitting funds across wallets: the attacker must either build a real history on each one or persuade trusted agents to risk their own standing. Whether the network is a haven, an island, or a mesa, this gate makes a Sybil attack costly in time, locked capital, and compromised reputations.
